guide.summary: Dropbox documents OAuth 2.0 for apps that act on behalf of users. Register a scoped app with App folder access and files.metadata.read, which the documented list_folder endpoint requires. Test first with a generated short-lived token, then with a user OAuth token from a test customer account. Do not enable content scopes. Production distribution review requirements are not established by the supplied sources and remain unknown.

steps.title: Create a scoped Dropbox app with App folder access
steps.detail: In the App Console, create a scoped-access app with App folder access. On the Permissions tab, enable files.metadata.read and submit the change. Expected: the app shows files.metadata.read and no content scopes.
steps.doneWhen: The app exists with App folder access and files.metadata.read is saved, with no content scopes enabled.

steps.title: Test list_folder with a generated short-lived token
steps.detail: Generate a short-lived token in the app Settings tab for the representative test account. Call list_folder with path empty and recursive false. Expected: JSON with entries containing .tag and name, plus cursor and has_more. Boundary check: confirm the response lists only names and metadata, and that the app's granted scopes contain only files.metadata.read.
steps.doneWhen: list_folder returns entries for the test account and the granted scopes are confirmed as files.metadata.read only.
